Subject: Kickoff: Emerald Systems - Private Deploy / Network Readout

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to align on next steps for the private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints + on-prem package). Our infra team at Emerald has a couple of hard requirements: non-overlapping CIDRs with our core VPC, traffic egress via our transit gateway, and a maintenance window for the initial sync.

Can your team share an implementation milestone plan and a network readout template we can review with our network ops and Acro (our edge vendor)? Attached is our current network diagram for reference.

High level questions we want answered in the plan:
- Public IPs / NAT expectations for outbound model calls
- Whether Redwood will require BGP or static routes for peering
- Firewall ACLs and port lists for private endpoints
- Staging vs prod CIDR separation and canary rollout guidance

Joe and I are available next Tuesday afternoon PT for a 45-minute technical review.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Infrastructure, Emerald Systems
(samira.khan@emeraldsys.com)

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Emerald Systems - Private Deploy / Network Readout

Samira —

Thanks for the clear list. I've pulled together a short milestone plan and a lightweight network readout template (see attached SOW and diagram). High-level notes up front:

- Redwood supports both static-route peering and BGP for the private link; for Emerald we recommend static for the initial staging cutover and BGP for prod if you want dynamic failover.
- Outbound model calls can egress over your transit gateway; we do not require public egress IPs from your side unless you want service whitelisting at the vendor layer.
- Private endpoints require the following ports: 443 (HTTPS), 22 (optional for on-prem appliance management), and UDP 500/4500 if IPsec is used for legacy tunnels.
- We recommend separate /24s for staging and prod endpoints to avoid cache/kv collisions during canary.

Proposed milestone summary (short):
1) Network readout & CIDR sign-off — by Oct 8
2) Staging peering & private endpoint build — Oct 11–14
3) On-prem package install & smoke tests (Acro coordinate) — Oct 15–18
4) Canary traffic & monitoring validation — Oct 19–20
5) Prod cutover window (maintenance) — Oct 21 02:00–05:00 PT

I'll block Tuesday 10/6 2:30pm PT for the technical review you suggested — does that work? Rishi will bring the IP templates and firewall stanzas.

Cheers,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Emerald Systems - Private Deploy / Network Readout

Samira / team —

Attaching a concise IP and routing template below and adding a few implementation constraints we typically see:  

Suggested CIDR allocations (examples):
- Emerald prod endpoint subnet: 10.20.10.0/24
- Emerald staging endpoint subnet: 10.20.20.0/24
- Redwood service-facing subnet (we host the endpoint IPs in your VPC): 10.20.11.0/28 (ephemeral IPs for LB)

Routing options:
- Static routes (preferred for initial cut): we exchange the exact /28 or /24 route and you add a route to your TGW to point to our peer attachment.
- BGP (recommended for multi-AZ failover): we can offer an iBGP session across the private link if you want propagation.

Firewall / ACLs:
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to 10.20.11.0/28
- Allow inbound from Acro vendor IPs for management (list attached in emerald_peering_cfg.txt)

On-prem package notes:
- The appliance requires 4 vCPU / 16GB RAM and 120GB disk for logs/cache.
- Management plane uses a separate mgmt endpoint; recommend NATing management to your corp network.

Open items I will bring to the call: exact ASN (if you want BGP), whether you want MTU bump for jumbo frames, and preferred monitoring hooks (we can push metrics to your Prometheus or use our Console integrations).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

1) We prefer static for initial staging (agreed). For prod we will plan BGP with our network team; ASN is 64521.
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood needs an egress NAT for control-plane telemetry (we want to avoid opening public egress where possible).

Acro (cc) — can you confirm the appliance sizing and any special port requirements on your side?

Lauren — 10/6 at 2:30pm PT works for us. Please send the calendar invite.

Samira
